title: Using a Free-plan AWS account without a surprise bill
summary: An off-site watchdog and this site's hosting on an AWS Free-plan account, built in Terraform with guardrails, one blocked auth method and a dated exit plan.

stat.label: a month for the off-site watchdog: one function, one table and one schedule rule

sections.heading: Problem
paragraphs: My lab runs on hardware in my home, so a power or internet outage silences the monitoring that would report it. I wanted a watcher outside the house, and a home for this site, on an AWS account with credit that expires in spring 2027.

sections.heading: What I built
paragraphs: The watchdog is one Lambda function. The lab sends it a heartbeat every two minutes. A scheduled run of the same function posts a message to my Discord when the heartbeat stops, and probes the lab's public endpoints. It uses one on-demand table, one schedule rule and three parameters, and I wrote it in Terraform like the rest of the lab.

The site is a private S3 bucket behind CloudFront with origin access control and a certificate. A custom response-headers policy sets a content security policy and HSTS. DNS stays at Cloudflare, so the account uses no Route 53. The module is written so it stays inside the always-free allowance.

I wrote the account rules down before the first resource existed. No AWS Organization, no Control Tower and no advanced features, because any of them ends credit earning. Free-plan-eligible services only, at the smallest sizes. A permissions boundary on the Terraform user stops it from creating a role more powerful than itself. A small monthly budget watches real money, a second budget counts credit burn, and anomaly detection emails me.

sections.heading: Trade-off
paragraphs: The deploy pipeline was designed around GitHub's OIDC login, so no long-lived key would exist. The account's organization has a service control policy that denies creating an OIDC provider, and a Free-plan account cannot lift it. I changed the design instead of working around the policy. The deploy identity is now a deploy-only IAM user with the same narrow policy. Terraform never creates its access key, so no secret reaches state. A script I run by hand creates the key and stores it as secrets on a protected environment that only the main branch may deploy to.
That is a weaker design than OIDC, and I chose it knowingly. The key can be rotated with one command, and the module switches back to OIDC with one variable on any account that allows it.

sections.heading: Result
paragraphs: The watchdog is deployed. The lab's heartbeat reaches it, and its daily "alive" message arrived in my Discord on 3 November.

The site deploys from a merge to the main branch. The first deploy ran on 3 November: it type-checked, tested and built the site, confirmed which identity it ran as, synced the built files to S3 and invalidated the CloudFront cache. I then read the site back through CloudFront's own address: the home page and the case-study pages return 200 with the HSTS header, and a missing page returns the 404 page. The read-back also found that extensionless URLs such as /work return 404, because the build writes work.html. No link on the site uses that form, so nothing breaks today, but I still have to fix it.

What is not done: the pdlab.dev domain still points at Cloudflare. The certificate validation record and the DNS cutover wait on my go-ahead, so visitors do not reach the AWS copy yet. The access key for the deploy user is a stopgap, and replacing it with a short-lived credential from Vault is a tracked follow-up.

sections.heading: What I would do differently
paragraphs: Check the account's policy limits before designing the auth. A short test that tries to create the OIDC provider would have found the block on the first day.

The exit plan is dated. The Free plan ends in April 2027, and a reminder fires two weeks before. By then I either upgrade with a budget alert in place, which should cost cents a month for a static site, or move the site to free static hosting and delete the bucket and distribution so nothing bills.
